A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WiserUI-Bench study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original MLLM evaluations, reasoning-strategy experiments and a 55-participant study of synthetic UI pairs.

after.justification: v4 retains original MLLM evaluations and reports additional performance breakdowns by UI change type.

M1.justification: The model inference procedures and evaluated reasoning strategies remain substantively unchanged. Renaming rationale alignment to interpretation and clarifying its prompts do not introduce a new model or algorithm; annotation-protocol revisions are assessed separately.

E1.justification: v4 removes the synthetic-UI evaluation covering 10 behavioral objectives and 55 human participants from v3 Section 7 and Appendix F, eliminating a distinct evaluation scenario. The 300-pair real-world benchmark and both core tasks remain. The revised industry taxonomy alone does not establish additional underlying data coverage.

E2.justification: The synthetic-pair comparison involving GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Qwen2.5-VL-32B and InternVL-2.5-38B disappears with v3 Table 5. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark experiments is unchanged, including all nine MLLMs and the reasoning strategies. JitterWeb's removal from Table 1 concerns a descriptive benchmark comparison, not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: v4 introduces evaluation partitions for Interactive Control, Content & State Display, Container & Layout Structure and Mixed cases, containing 100, 79, 49 and 72 instances. Its annotation account also shifts from collaborative review to independent two-of-three retention, with subsequent UX-law tagging. These are reported protocol revisions; the PDFs do not establish reannotation or rerunning of the main experiments. Core model configurations and input-order evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds analysis of selection performance across functional UI change types and replaces the main selection example with three InternVL-2.5-38B cases distinguishing perception errors from behavioral-reasoning errors (Figure 6). Synthetic-study case analyses disappear. The reasoning-strategy analysis, UX-dimension analysis and four retained appendix examples are matched across relocation and renumbering.

E5.justification: v4 newly quantifies expert agreement: 562 retained interpretations had unanimous agreement and 122 had two-expert agreement, from 845 initial candidates. Three-run averaging and standard-deviation reporting remain unchanged for retained experiments. The revised evaluator accuracy and kappa values are numerical result changes, not a new statistical procedure.

E6.justification: v4 adds type-specific results, including GPT-4o consistent accuracy of 17.69% on layout cases and 37.50% on Mixed cases, while removing synthetic-study model scores, human votes and associated deviations. Evaluator validation changes from 70.8% accuracy and kappa 0.42 to 83.0% and 0.66 without explaining the revision. Industry statistics also change under revised categories, including retail from 43.0% to 22.0%. Aggregate benchmark, reasoning-strategy and text-similarity scores remain identical.

T1.justification: The UX-law descriptions, cognitive grouping and random-guessing argument for consistent accuracy remain unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs; v4's abductive framing and revised UI taxonomy are conceptual explanations.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central contributions: a real-world A/B-tested UI benchmark with expert annotations, two evaluation tasks and evidence of limited behavioral understanding in current MLLMs. Post-hoc explanation was already explicit in v3, so the interpretation terminology does not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly frames explanations as abductive interpretations of aggregate outcomes and softens v3's description of some outputs as expert-level explanations. It adds interpretations of UI-type differences and removes the detailed DPO-based generation proposal. Limitations additionally discuss the infeasibility of independently conducting comparable production-scale A/B tests; cultural-bias and interactive-UI limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v4 documents the initial annotation pool, agreement-based retention and element-versus-attribute counting rules, and announces a planned noncommercial research license. Synthetic-study instructions and implementation details disappear. Model identifiers, temperature, hardware, software versions and the benchmark repository reference remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Hobbs et al., Bhagavatula et al. and Quin et al. to support abductive interpretation and A/B-testing context. It removes the generation and preference-optimization discussion and associated citations. The central positioning against existing UI benchmarks, visual-reasoning benchmarks and behavioral agents remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial narrative passages are rewritten, with interpretation and recall terminology adopted throughout. Reasoning-strategy and UX-dimension analyses move into the experiments section; discussion and conclusion are separated; limitations and ethics move into the main text. The appendices are reorganized, and author and affiliation information changes.

P2.justification: v4 substantially reformats the document, expands Table 2 into a wide table with category columns and colored highlights, redraws the curation pipeline and reorganizes dataset charts. It introduces a new selection-case display and separates the retained interpretation example. Human-study tables and figures disappear, while most appendix prompts and examples remain with revised sizing and numbering.

improvement.justification: v4 improves the central benchmark's clarity and diagnostic value through explicit annotation-agreement reporting, clearer recall terminology, UI-type breakdowns and more structured failure analysis. It also tempers the earlier expert-level characterization. Removing the small synthetic-UI study narrows supporting evidence, and the unexplained evaluator-validation increase cannot establish an improved evaluator. The clearest net gains concern interpretation and documentation of the retained study.
